title: The Button That Was Too Easy to Press
title_ja: 押しやすすぎたボタン
fact_notes: 人物・出来事・制度は架空の教材例。実在の調査・統計・実証結果ではない。制作台帳は来歴確認用。

sentences.en: Suppose a group of students designs a digital notice board for an imaginary school, allowing teachers to send announcements to selected classes.
sentences.ja: 架空の学校で教師が選択したクラスに告知を送れるデジタル掲示板を生徒が設計するとしよう。

sentences.en: The team places a large publication button at the bottom of the editing screen so that teachers can quickly complete their work.
sentences.ja: 教師がすぐ作業を終えられるよう編集画面下に大きな公開ボタンを置く。

sentences.en: During a demonstration, a teacher accidentally publishes an unfinished announcement while trying to save a draft of the message.
sentences.ja: 実演中教師は下書きを保存しようとして未完成の告知を誤って公開する。

sentences.en: The mistake prompts the designers to reconsider whether reducing the number of steps always makes a system easier to use.
sentences.ja: 手順を減らせば常に使いやすくなるかを設計者が再考するきっかけになる。

sentences.en: The students initially suggest adding a confirmation message before every operation performed through the notice board.
sentences.ja: 最初は掲示板での全操作前に確認メッセージを追加する案を出す。

sentences.en: However, another student points out that repeated warnings might interrupt ordinary tasks and encourage users to dismiss messages without reading them.
sentences.ja: しかし警告の反復で通常作業が中断され、利用者が読まずに閉じるようになるかもしれないと指摘する。

sentences.en: The team therefore distinguishes between reversible editing actions and operations that immediately affect other people.
sentences.ja: そこで取り消せる編集操作と直ちに他者へ影響する操作を区別する。

sentences.en: They consider how the interface could draw particular attention to decisions whose consequences would be difficult to reverse.
sentences.ja: 取り消しにくい結果を持つ判断に画面が特に注意を向けさせる方法を考える。

sentences.en: The revised prototype separates saving and publishing into clearly labeled controls and displays the intended audience before publication.
sentences.ja: 修正版は保存と公開を明示した操作に分け、公開前に対象者を表示する。

sentences.en: Users can also preview how an announcement will appear to its recipients instead of relying on the appearance of the editing screen.
sentences.ja: 編集画面の見え方だけでなく受信者への表示をプレビューできる。

sentences.en: For an ordinary draft, the system avoids unnecessary interruptions and provides an indication that recent changes have been preserved.
sentences.ja: 通常の下書きでは不要な中断を避け最近の変更が保存されたことを示す。

sentences.en: The students test several fictional tasks to examine whether each control communicates the intended action rather than simply appearing attractive.
sentences.ja: 各操作が見た目の魅力だけでなく意図した動作を伝えるか架空の課題で調べる。

sentences.en: One remaining difficulty concerns announcements that have already reached their recipients before an error is discovered.
sentences.ja: 残る困難は誤りが判明する前に受信者に届いた告知に関係する。

sentences.en: Removing a message from the notice board does not necessarily erase the information from people's memories or prevent them from acting on it.
sentences.ja: 掲示板から削除しても記憶から消したり行動を防いだりできるとは限らない。

sentences.en: The team therefore designs a correction procedure that makes the revised information distinguishable from the earlier version.
sentences.ja: そこで修正情報を以前の版と区別できる訂正手順を設計する。

sentences.en: They acknowledge that a classroom prototype cannot prove the security or reliability of a real communication system.
sentences.ja: 試作では実際の通信システムの安全性や信頼性は証明できないと認める。

sentences.en: The example illustrates that convenient design requires more than minimizing the effort associated with every individual action.
sentences.ja: 便利な設計には個々の操作の労力を最小にするだけでは足りないことを示す。

sentences.en: A carefully placed extra step may support users when it draws attention to a significant and potentially irreversible decision.
sentences.ja: 重要で取り消し不能かもしれない判断に注意を向ける追加手順は利用者を支援し得る。

sentences.en: The value of that step depends on whether it communicates relevant information at the appropriate moment.
sentences.ja: その手順の価値は適切な時点に関連情報を伝えるかによる。

sentences.en: Responsible interface design balances efficiency with the user's ability to understand and control the consequences of an action.
sentences.ja: 責任ある画面設計は効率と操作結果を理解し制御する能力の均衡を取る。

vocabulary.definition: elements used to operate a system

questions.prompt: What is the board designed for?

options: A completed notice was saved correctly.

questions.prompt: What distinction did the team make?
options: Reversible edits versus actions affecting others.
To guarantee all notices are accurate.
To see the recipients' view before release.

questions.prompt: What problem can remain after deletion?
options: People may remember or act on the message.
All readers lose access to school.
To clarify which information replaces the earlier version.
To prove the system is secure.
Design should balance ease of use with awareness of consequential actions.
All actions should require one click.
questions.explanation_ja: 効率と結果の理解を両立。

grammar.focus: whether reducing the number of steps
instead of relying on the appearance

paraphrases.source: The mistake prompts the designers to reconsider whether reducing the number of steps always makes a system easier to use.
paraphrases.rewrite: The mistake led the team to question whether fewer steps always improve usability.

paraphrases.source: However, another student points out that repeated warnings might interrupt ordinary tasks and encourage users to dismiss messages without reading them.
paraphrases.rewrite: Frequent alerts might train people to close them unread.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 警告を読まなくなる可能性。

paraphrases.source: Users can also preview how an announcement will appear to its recipients instead of relying on the appearance of the editing screen.
paraphrases.rewrite: A preview lets users see what recipients will see, not just the editing view.

paraphrases.source: A carefully placed extra step may support users when it draws attention to a significant and potentially irreversible decision.
paraphrases.rewrite: An additional step can help if it highlights a consequential decision.
